items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: Yeah, in the Southern, uh, Syncopators... the sax section was... Joe Ruzon.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. Now, uh, who was in this Southern Syncopators? Can you remember, man?

Yeah, in the Southern, uh, Syncopators, there was, uh, Eddie Pearson on trombone, Leo Dejo trumpet, and a trumpet player named DeRuxa, DeRuxa, DeRuxa from over the river. Mm-hmm. And the sax section was, uh, Elliot Taylor. Mm-hmm. Uh, Arthur Durbney, Joe Ruzon. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. And, uh, rhythm section was Sidney Montague, I believe Booker Washington on bass, and Allegretto on piano.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: And the sax section was Joe Ruzon on tenor... And the rhythm section was me... Alec Grutter was doing most of the arrangement... That was Peter on band, second. That was his, that was his. Wait, Violin rhythm? Yeah, he was the leader of the band. His band.

ctx.x: You never did join the WPA band then?

No, I was going to say, I always thought that was a little too slow money for me. I, I, well I should have because there wasn't nothing to it, you know. Most of the guys got in just for the money of it, you see. But like I say, then I was doing a little range, I was selling arrangements around you and everything, you know. But I, I, in other words, I was doing it just as good as those guys there, you see. So, and then another thing I, I didn't like it because the time that, like, you would get a good job, it…
